title: The Owl and the World-Soul: from the Stift chamber at Tübingen to the grave beside Fichte
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Stuttgart, birth in the Eberhardstraße
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In a sixteenth-century house on the Eberhardstraße, in the capital of the small Lutheran Duchy of Württemberg, a son is born to Georg Ludwig Hegel, secretary at the ducal Rentkammer, and to Maria Magdalena his wife. They christen him Georg Wilhelm Friedrich. The duchy is administered by families exactly like this one: men who keep a prince's accounts and send their sons into the church or the civil service. In the same year, far to the northeast at Königsberg, Immanuel Kant declines a chair offered him by the university of Jena and stays where he is.
suggested_refs: The Hegel-Haus at Eberhardstraße 53, Stuttgart, the birth house, museum since 1991

stops.name: Stuttgart, the Gymnasium illustre
stops.date_confidence: year attested for entry to the Gymnasium; month and day defaulted. The school is named here as it was named in 1776: the Gymnasium illustre, founded 1686, which takes the title Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium only later.
stops.campa: At three he is put into the German School, at five into the Latin School, and at six into the Gymnasium illustre, the ducal school of the capital. He reads Sophocles and Epictetus, copies whole passages into a diary of extracts, and is remembered by his teachers less for brilliance than for a plodding and total thoroughness. The habit never leaves him. Everything he will later write is built the same way, one exhausted step after another, with nothing skipped and nothing taken on trust.
suggested_refs: The Stuttgart Gymnasium illustre and Hegel's schoolboy diary of extracts

stops.name: Stuttgart, the death of the mother
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not established in the sources consulted
stops.campa: Maria Magdalena Hegel dies of a bilious fever. Her son is thirteen. The house she leaves holds a father in the ducal accounts office, a younger sister, Christiane, and a younger brother, Georg Ludwig, who will die thirty years on as an officer in Napoleon's Russian campaign. Christiane will outlive the philosopher by a few months and drown herself. Hegel goes back to his extracts. He will build a system in which nothing that happens is wasted and everything that passes is kept inside what comes after it.
suggested_refs: The Hegel family household in Stuttgart after 1783

stops.name: Tübingen, entering the Tübinger Stift
stops.date_confidence: 1788 per en.wikipedia; October is the customary term start and the day is defaulted. The atlas file schelling.journey.json instead dates Hegel's entry to 18 October 1790; the contradiction is left standing and both stops are carried.
stops.campa: Eighteen years old, he enters the Tübinger Stift, the Protestant seminary of the duchy, on a ducal scholarship that binds him to the church. The Stift is a converted Augustinian house on the Neckar, cold, strictly ruled, and packed with the ablest boys in Württemberg, nearly all of them destined for pulpits and few of them wanting one. He matriculates in theology and philosophy at the university. Within two years the two men whose names will be tied to his for two centuries are sleeping in the same room.
suggested_refs: The Tübinger Stift on the Neckar, seminary of the Duchy of Württemberg

stops.name: Tübingen, the Stift, the shared chamber
stops.date_confidence: 18 October 1790 as fixed by schelling.journey.json, whose pin is inherited here unchanged; Hegel's own record has him in the Stift since 1788, and the two datings are not reconciled
stops.campa: One narrow chamber holds three. Hegel, who takes his Master of Arts this year; Friedrich Hölderlin, who will bend the German language into a shape it has not had before; and Friedrich Schelling, fifteen years old and already the prodigy of the house. They read Kant by candlelight, and Plato, and Spinoza, inside a seminary that means to make village pastors of them. Kant is alive at Königsberg, sixty-six, and knows nothing about it. Nothing in the arrangement of the room says which of the three is the philosopher.
suggested_refs: The attic chamber of the Tübinger Stift shared by Hegel, Hölderlin and Schelling

stops.name: Tübingen, the tree of liberty in the meadow
stops.date_confidence: traditional. The date comes from schelling.journey.json, which carries the planting as attested; the verification pass finds no contemporary evidence for the tree, calls it a later legend, and notes that the geography lens's own wording concedes as much.
stops.campa: On the fourth anniversary of the Bastille the three go out into a meadow by the Neckar, plant a tree of liberty, dance around it, and swear fidelity to freedom and to the French Revolution. Hegel is twenty-three and licensed to preach in a duchy that answers to a duke. Thirty years later, from a chair in the Prussian capital, he will be accused of having sold that morning for a state salary, and he will answer that the principle of the Revolution was reason and that reason is what a state is for.
suggested_refs: The Neckar meadow at Tübingen and the Freiheitsbaum of 14 July 1793

stops.name: Tübingen, the examinations and the leaving
stops.date_confidence: September 1793 per Deutsche Biographie; day defaulted
stops.campa: He sits his magisterial and theological examinations and takes the certificate that licenses him to preach. The examiners note a decent grasp of theology, an industrious character, and middling promise in philosophy. He never enters a pulpit. The duchy has trained him for a career he declines in the week he qualifies for it, and the only work open to a licensed candidate who refuses the church is the teaching of other men's children in other men's houses, which is what he does for the next eight years.
suggested_refs: The Tübingen examination records of the 1793 class of the Stift

stops.name: Bern, tutor in the house of von Steiger
stops.date_confidence: 1793 attested; the month is inferred from the September departure from Tübingen and the day is defaulted
stops.campa: He crosses into the Swiss cantons as Hofmeister, house tutor to the children of Captain Karl Friedrich von Steiger, a Bernese patrician. The work is genteel servitude: he eats with the family and is not of it. In the hours he keeps for himself he reads Kant through, and political economy, and the constitutions of the cantons, and he writes on religion, on the difference between a faith commanded and a faith arrived at. None of it is published. He is twenty-three, unknown, and a long way from anyone who knows him.
suggested_refs: The von Steiger town house at Bern, where Hegel served as Hofmeister 1793-1796

stops.name: Tschugg, the summers at the Steiger estate
stops.date_confidence: the Steiger summers of 1793-1796 are attested as a period; the single July 1794 date is a placeholder inside it. Coordinates corrected to the village of Tschugg, 47° 1′ 38″ N, 7° 4′ 37″ E; the earlier pin lay some nine kilometres off near Gals.
stops.campa: The family removes for the summer months to its country estate at Tschugg above the Bielersee, and the tutor comes with it. Here, in a landed house among vines, he drafts the manuscripts on religion that stay in his desk unpublished the whole of his life. The estate outlasts everyone in it: since 1889 the old Landgut Steiger has been a clinic. Hegel walks the lake, writes what nobody will read for a century, and waits for a letter from Hölderlin that will get him out of Switzerland.
suggested_refs: The Landgut Steiger at Tschugg, since 1889 the Klinik Bethesda

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the house of the wine merchant Gogel
stops.date_confidence: 1797 attested for the Frankfurt post; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: The letter comes. Hölderlin, tutoring in Frankfurt, finds him a place in the household of Johann Noe Gogel, a wine merchant, and the two friends of the Stift chamber are in one city again. Hegel writes The Spirit of Christianity and Its Fate here in 1799 and does not publish it; in it history stops being a record of what men happened to believe and becomes the thing that makes believing possible at all. He is twenty-nine, tutoring, unpublished. These are the last years in which he is nobody.
suggested_refs: The Gogel household at Frankfurt am Main and the unpublished theological manuscripts of 1797-1800

stops.name: Stuttgart, the death of the father
stops.date_confidence: January 1799 per de.wikipedia; day not established. The chronology lens tagged this event as tradition; it is attested, and the geography lens already had it so.
stops.campa: Georg Ludwig Hegel, secretary of the ducal Rentkammer, dies in Stuttgart in January. The estate divided among the three surviving children is modest, and it is enough. Hegel gives notice to the Gogel household. A man who has spent six years in other people's houses teaching other people's children has for the first time an income that answers to nobody, and he spends it on the only thing he wants, which is a university. He writes to Schelling, who is at Jena and famous at twenty-four.
suggested_refs: The estate of Georg Ludwig Hegel, Rentkammersekretär of Württemberg, divided 1799

stops.name: Jena, the habilitation and the first book
stops.date_confidence: January 1801 per the geography lens; day defaulted
stops.campa: Schelling, called to Jena by Goethe at twenty-three, tells him to come, and he comes. He submits a Latin dissertation on the orbits of the planets, habilitates, and becomes Privatdozent: unsalaried, paid only what students choose to hand him at the door. The town is the loudest philosophical place in Europe. Fichte was driven out of it two years ago over atheism, Schiller held the chair of history here, Novalis and the Schlegels met here in 1799. Hegel's first book defends Schelling against Fichte.
suggested_refs: De Orbitis Planetarum, the 1801 habilitation dissertation, and The Difference between Fichte's and Schelling's System of Philosophy

stops.name: Jena, the Kritisches Journal der Philosophie
stops.date_confidence: 1802 attested; the journal runs 1802-1803; month and day defaulted. The chronology lens misspelled the title as Kritische Journal; the correct form is used here.
stops.campa: Hegel and Schelling found the Kritisches Journal der Philosophie and print its essays unsigned, so that the pieces read as the work of one philosophy rather than of two philosophers. The device holds for two years and conceals, while it holds, a widening difference: Schelling's absolute is reached at a stroke by intellectual intuition, Hegel's has to be walked to, and the walking turns out to be the whole of it. Friedrich Fröbel had matriculated at the same university three years earlier.
suggested_refs: The Kritisches Journal der Philosophie, Jena 1802-1803, essays published unsigned

stops.name: Jena, extraordinary professor without a salary
stops.date_confidence: 1805 attested; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: On Goethe's recommendation from Weimar he is made extraordinary professor, which raises his title and not his pay. Schelling has gone to Würzburg and the letters between them thin out. Hegel is thirty-five: one book, a run of journal essays, no salary, no chair, no wife, and a manuscript growing on the desk that he has not yet settled a name for. He writes it against a printer's deadline and against a war walking toward Thuringia from the west, and he finishes it with about a day to spare.
suggested_refs: Goethe's correspondence with the Weimar ministry on the Jena appointments

stops.name: Jena, Napoleon rides through the town
stops.date_confidence: attested. The chronology lens filed this together with the battle under 14 October; Napoleon entered Jena on the thirteenth, the day before, and Hegel's letter is dated the thirteenth.
stops.campa: The French come into Jena on the thirteenth, the day before the battle. Hegel stands in the street and watches the Emperor ride out of the city on reconnaissance, and writes to his friend Niethammer that night. The phrase the next two centuries will quote, the world-spirit on horseback, is not in the letter. What he actually writes is stranger and more exact: a world-soul, on a horse, in a street, at an hour, doing a particular piece of military work. The man about to argue that history is reasonable has just watched it ride past.
stops.quote: I saw the Emperor, this world-soul, riding out of the city on reconnaissance.
stops.quote_source: Hegel, letter to Niethammer, Jena, 13 October 1806, marxists.org Hegel Archive
suggested_refs: Hegel's letter to Friedrich Immanuel Niethammer, 13 October 1806

stops.name: Jena, the Phenomenology finished as the battle opens
stops.date_confidence: the battle is 14 October 1806, attested. Whether the last pages of the manuscript went to the printer just before, during, or just after it is disputed among biographers and is not settled here.
stops.campa: On the fourteenth Napoleon breaks the Prussian army at Jena while Davout, twelve miles off at Auerstedt, destroys its main body without either commander knowing until evening. On the plateau where Fichte once lectured on the free self, the old Prussian state ceases for years to exist. In the town below, Hegel gets the last pages of the Phenomenology of Spirit out of the house. French soldiers are billeted in his rooms. The book says that a consciousness becomes itself only by being recognised by another.
stops.quote: Self-consciousness exists in itself and for itself, in that, and by the fact that it exists for another self-consciousness; that is to say, it is only by being acknowledged or 'recognized'.
stops.quote_source: G.W.F. Hegel, Phenomenology of Spirit, Lordship and Bondage, para. 178, marxists.org Hegel Archive
suggested_refs: The Jena-Auerstedt battlefield, 14 October 1806
The manuscript of the Phänomenologie des Geistes, sent to Goebhardt at Bamberg

stops.name: Jena, the son of the landlady
stops.date_confidence: 5 February 1807 per de.wikipedia, corroborated by the boy joining the household in April 1817 aged about ten. The chronology lens gave February 1806; that reading is rejected here and recorded.
stops.campa: Christina Charlotte Burkhardt, born Fischer, Hegel's landlady, bears him a son, and the child is registered Georg Ludwig Friedrich Fischer, under her name. Hegel pays for him and does not acknowledge him. Ten years will pass before the boy enters his father's house at Heidelberg, after his mother's death, and twenty-four before he dies in the Dutch service at Batavia, a few months ahead of the father who never gave him the name. The philosopher of recognition withholds it here.
suggested_refs: The Jena baptismal register entry for Georg Ludwig Friedrich Fischer, February 1807

stops.name: Bamberg, the editor of the Bamberger Zeitung
stops.date_confidence: he leaves Jena in March 1807 per Deutsche Biographie and takes the Bamberg post the same year; the day is defaulted
stops.campa: Jena's enrolment collapses after the battle and its Privatdozent has no income at all. Niethammer, the friend the Napoleon letter was written to, finds him a newspaper. For a year and a half the author of the Phenomenology of Spirit edits the Bamberger Zeitung, setting French army bulletins in type and correcting the war news of the man he watched ride past. The book itself appears in 1807 from Joseph Anton Goebhardt, credited to Bamberg and Würzburg, and is read by almost nobody.
stops.quote_source: G.W.F. Hegel, Phenomenology of Spirit, Preface, marxists.org Hegel Archive (translator not credited on the fetched page)
suggested_refs: The offices of the Bamberger Zeitung
The 1807 Goebhardt first edition of the Phänomenologie des Geistes

stops.name: Nuremberg, rector of the Ägidiengymnasium
stops.date_confidence: November 1808 per de.wikipedia and the chronology lens; the geography lens gives December 1808 and the disagreement is left standing. Day defaulted. The pin is the historic school on the Egidienplatz, not the 1911 building of its successor.
stops.campa: Niethammer, now in the Bavarian education ministry, makes him rector of the Ägidiengymnasium on the Egidienplatz, and for eight years the most difficult philosopher in Europe teaches logic to schoolboys and signs their reports. The classroom does what no salary had done: it forces him to say the whole thing in order, from the beginning, at a speed a boy of fourteen can follow. The propaedeutic he dictates there is the first draft of the system, tested on the one audience that shows when a sentence has failed.
suggested_refs: The Ägidiengymnasium at Egidienplatz 10, Nuremberg, and the Philosophische Propädeutik dictated to its pupils

stops.name: Nuremberg, the marriage to Marie von Tucher
stops.date_confidence: 1811 attested, September per the geography lens, day defaulted. The venue of the ceremony is not established in the sources consulted and the pin is central Nuremberg.
stops.campa: He marries Marie Helena Susanna von Tucher, eldest daughter of a Nuremberg senator, of one of the patrician houses whose names are on the walls of the town. He is forty-one and a provincial schoolmaster with one book behind him. The match steadies the finances and the household at once, and the household is what the next twenty years of writing rest on. Two sons will be born here within three years, and a third boy, alive in Jena and unacknowledged, waits outside the arrangement.
suggested_refs: The Tucher family of Nuremberg and the marriage of September 1811

stops.name: Nuremberg, the Science of Logic
stops.date_confidence: 1812 for the first volume, attested; the three volumes appear 1812, 1813 and 1816. Month and day defaulted. The brother's death in Russia is attested for 1812, but no place precise enough to pin was found, so it is carried in this stop.
stops.campa: The first volume of the Science of Logic goes to press, the second in 1813, the third in 1816. It opens with being, which turns out on inspection to be indistinguishable from nothing, and the entire system walks out of that first failure. He writes it in the evenings after the school day, in the town where he corrects Latin exercises for a living. In the same year his brother Georg Ludwig, an officer in Napoleon's army, marches into Russia with the Grande Armée and does not come back.
suggested_refs: The Wissenschaft der Logik, Nuremberg 1812-1816, first edition

stops.name: Nuremberg, the two sons
stops.date_confidence: Karl born 1813 and Immanuel 1814, both attested by year; months and days not established, and the stop is dated to the earlier birth
stops.campa: Karl Friedrich Wilhelm is born in 1813 and Immanuel Thomas Christian in 1814. Karl will become a historian of the medieval German towns and will spend part of his life editing his father; Immanuel will go into theology and the Prussian church administration. Between them they keep the manuscripts, the lecture notes and the letters. Nearly everything printed under their father's name after 1831 has passed through the hands of one or other of them first.
suggested_refs: The papers of Karl Hegel, historian, and Immanuel Hegel, kept and edited after 1831

stops.name: Heidelberg, the first ordinary chair
stops.date_confidence: October 1816 per en.wikipedia and Deutsche Biographie; day defaulted
stops.campa: At forty-six he gets his first proper professorship. Heidelberg offers, Erlangen offers, Berlin hesitates, and he takes Heidelberg and starts lecturing on aesthetics and on the history of philosophy: the courses, given from notes and never published by him, that will do more for his fame than any book he prints in his lifetime. The schoolmastering is over. He has been eight years out of a university and walks back into one with a finished system in his luggage.
suggested_refs: The University of Heidelberg lecture lists for the winter semester of 1816

stops.name: Heidelberg, the Encyclopaedia of the Philosophical Sciences
stops.date_confidence: 1817 attested; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He publishes the Encyclopaedia of the Philosophical Sciences in Basic Outline, the whole system compressed into numbered paragraphs so that a student can hold it in one hand while the lecturer talks around it. Logic, then the philosophy of nature, then the philosophy of spirit, in that order because the order is the argument. He will revise it twice more, in 1827 and in 1830, each time longer. It is the only place where the entire architecture stands complete between two covers.
suggested_refs: The Enzyklopädie der philosophischen Wissenschaften im Grundrisse, Heidelberg 1817

stops.name: Heidelberg, Ludwig Fischer enters the house
stops.date_confidence: April 1817 attested. That the boy is about ten at this date is what fixes his birth to 1807 rather than 1806.
stops.campa: The boy born to the Jena landlady, about ten years old and orphaned by his mother's death, is brought into the Hegel household and raised alongside Karl and Immanuel. He keeps the name Fischer. Marie takes him in without any recorded complaint, and the father who has paid for him for ten years now has him at the table. The arrangement lasts a few years. It ends with the young man enlisting in the Dutch colonial service and dying at Batavia in the last year of his father's life.
suggested_refs: The Hegel household at Heidelberg, 1817, with three boys in it

stops.name: Berlin, the chair on Unter den Linden
stops.date_confidence: October 1818 attested. The institution is named here as it was named in 1818: the University of Berlin, which becomes the Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität only in 1828 and the Humboldt-Universität in 1949.
stops.campa: He takes the chair of philosophy at the University of Berlin, the institution that is not yet called the Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität and will not carry Humboldt's name for another hundred and thirty years. The chair was Fichte's, the university's first elected rector, four years dead. Hegel holds it until he dies. Within a decade these lecture rooms are the centre of academic philosophy in the German states, and to have a position in philosophy means to be for or against one man.
suggested_refs: The university building at Unter den Linden 6, Berlin, and the chair held before him by Fichte

stops.name: Berlin, the house at the Kupfergraben
stops.date_confidence: the residence Am Kupfergraben is attested by the memorial plaque in Berlin-Mitte; the house number and the date of moving in are not established, and 1819 is a placeholder inside the Berlin years. The geography lens had marked this as unverified tradition before the plaque was found.
stops.campa: He keeps house by the Kupfergraben canal, a few minutes on foot from the lecture hall, and a memorial plaque in Berlin-Mitte marks the residence. Students come from Poland, Russia, Greece and Scandinavia to sit in rooms too small for them and take down, in notebooks later printed as books, the lectures on aesthetics, on religion, on the philosophy of history. Almost nothing on that posthumous shelf is a book he wrote. It is a room, transcribed by men who disagreed about what they had heard.
suggested_refs: The Gedenktafel Am Kupfergraben, Berlin-Mitte, marking Hegel's residence

stops.name: Berlin, the Philosophy of Right
stops.date_confidence: published 1820; the original title page dates it 1821 and both research lenses followed the title page. Month and day defaulted.
stops.campa: Elements of the Philosophy of Right is published, with the following year printed on the title page. It defends constitutional monarchy, a market restrained by corporations, trial by jury and a professional public administration, against reactionaries who want none of it and radicals who want all of it at once, and both sides read it as treason. The preface holds the sentence that will be quoted against him for two centuries, about the rational and the real, and the one nobody quotes against him, about the owl.
stops.quote: The owl of Minerva takes its flight only when the shades of night are gathering.
stops.quote_source: G.W.F. Hegel, Philosophy of Right, Preface, trans. S.W. Dyde (1896), marxists.org Hegel Archive
suggested_refs: Grundlinien der Philosophie des Rechts, published 1820 with an 1821 title page
sources: Wikipedia, 'Elements of the Philosophy of Right'
marxists.org Hegel Archive, Philosophy of Right preface

stops.name: Weimar, calling on Goethe
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia gives two trips to Weimar, the second ending in their last meeting; neither trip is dated in the sources consulted, and 1820 is a placeholder inside the Berlin decade. The geography lens's 'repeated visits' overstates the record.
stops.campa: Twice in the Berlin decade he goes to Weimar to call on Goethe, who is past seventy and who stands behind half the appointments of Hegel's life, at Jena and after. They correspond with formality and with care, the poet and the philosopher of the same small country, each having decided long ago that the other is necessary. On the second visit they see each other for the last time. Goethe outlives him by four months and dies at eighty-two, still at work.
suggested_refs: The Goethe-Hegel correspondence and the two Weimar visits of the Berlin years

stops.name: Amsterdam, the Dutch pictures
stops.date_confidence: 1822 attested for the journey to the northern Netherlands; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He travels to the northern Netherlands, to Amsterdam and The Hague, with Brussels on the same circuit, and stands in front of Dutch painting: kitchens, taverns, cattle, light on a plastered wall, made by a republic of merchants with no god and no king to commission anything. He refuses to call it a lesser art. A whole people, he decides, has arrived at the point of finding its ordinary life worth looking at, and the lectures on aesthetics carry that conclusion afterwards.
suggested_refs: The Dutch cabinet paintings seen in 1822 and the genre-painting sections of the Berlin aesthetics lectures

stops.name: Vienna, the opera every evening
stops.date_confidence: 1824 attested for the Vienna and Prague journey; month and day defaulted. The Rossini enthusiasm is widely repeated in the biographies and was not independently re-verified in this pass.
stops.campa: In Vienna the philosopher of the Absolute goes to the opera night after night and writes home in raptures about Rossini, which his Berlin students find impossible to square with anything he says from the lectern. He travels on to Prague in the same circuit through the Habsburg lands. He is fifty-four, famous, and at the head of a system that explains the necessity of everything, and he spends his evenings on Italian comedies about servants outwitting their masters.
suggested_refs: Hegel's 1824 letters from Vienna on the Italian opera

stops.name: Paris, the galleries of the Louvre
stops.date_confidence: 1827 attested for the one recorded Paris journey; the dates within the year were not established, so month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: He makes his one recorded journey to Paris and walks the galleries of the Louvre. The city is thirty-eight years past the Bastille and the tree in the Neckar meadow, and he writes of being struck by the scale and the assurance of French public life. He never sees it again. Sixteen years later a young Rhinelander named Karl Marx, expelled from Prussia, will reach the same city carrying a notebook of objections to the Philosophy of Right, and the argument will go on here without him.
suggested_refs: The Musée du Louvre galleries as seen in 1827

stops.name: Berlin, elected rector of the university
stops.date_confidence: October 1829 attested; the term ends in September 1830; day defaulted
stops.campa: The university elects him rector, its highest office, for a term of one year. He is fifty-nine. He was licensed to preach in Württemberg at twenty-three and never went into a pulpit. At thirty-seven he was correcting French war bulletins for a provincial newspaper at Bamberg. He now runs the leading university of the Prussian state and answers to its minister. He never quite becomes a court philosopher, but the distance between him and the throne has grown very short.
suggested_refs: The rectorate of the University of Berlin, October 1829 to September 1830

stops.name: Berlin, the tricentennial of the Augsburg Confession
stops.date_confidence: June 1830 per Deutsche Biographie as relayed by the geography lens; the text of the address was not reached and the claim stands as reconstruction. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: As rector he gives the public address for the three-hundredth anniversary of the Augsburg Confession, tying Luther's doctrine to the progress of the Protestant German states and to freedom of conscience as a political principle. A month later Paris rises again and puts a citizen king on the throne, and the old man at the lectern, who has spent his whole life saying that the Revolution was reason's own work, has to say in public what he makes of a second one.
suggested_refs: The rectoral address on the tricentenary of the Confessio Augustana, June 1830

stops.name: Batavia, the death of Ludwig Fischer
stops.date_confidence: 1831 attested for the death, shortly before Hegel's own; month, day and burial place are not established, and the pin is Batavia, the present-day Jakarta
stops.campa: In the Dutch East Indies, in the garrison town of Batavia, the son who was never given his father's name dies in the colonial service at twenty-four. The news travels by sailing ship and reaches Berlin slowly, if it reaches it in time at all. Hegel has some months left. The system holds that spirit is what recognises itself in another, and that nothing real is simply lost; the young man in the Batavia ground is the part of the life the system was never made to answer for.
suggested_refs: The Dutch colonial garrison rolls at Batavia, 1831

stops.name: Kreuzberg, out of the city while the cholera runs
stops.date_confidence: August 1831 attested; day defaulted. The Order of the Red Eagle is attested for 1831 without a month and is carried in this stop rather than pinned separately.
stops.campa: Cholera reaches Berlin in August and the city empties of everyone who can afford to go. Hegel takes lodgings in Kreuzberg, outside the old walls, and works there while the epidemic runs its course. In the same year King Frederick William III decorates him with the Order of the Red Eagle, third class, the Prussian state's acknowledgement of the philosopher it is accused of keeping. He is sixty-one. He means to lecture again as soon as the city is safe, and he does.
suggested_refs: The Berlin cholera epidemic of 1831
The Order of the Red Eagle, third class, conferred 1831

stops.name: Berlin, back for the new semester
stops.date_confidence: October 1831 attested; day defaulted
stops.campa: The epidemic slackens, he comes back into the city and opens the winter semester, apparently in good health. He is lecturing on the history of philosophy and on the proofs of the existence of God, and revising. He has held this chair thirteen years. The house at the Kupfergraben fills again with students who have nowhere else they would rather be, and everything about the autumn of 1831 has the shape of a man with a decade of work still in front of him.
suggested_refs: The Berlin winter semester lecture list of 1831

stops.name: Berlin, death at the Kupfergraben
stops.date_confidence: 14 November 1831 attested. The cause is contested between the contemporary cholera diagnosis and a later reading as a different gastrointestinal illness; neither is chosen here.
stops.campa: He dies on the afternoon of the fourteenth of November, sixty-one years old, in the house by the Kupfergraben. His physicians write cholera, the disease that is in the city; later scholarship suspects a different gastrointestinal illness, and the question has never been closed. Three years afterwards Heinrich Heine prints the line the century then repeats as a deathbed saying, that only one man ever understood him and that man did not understand him either.
stops.quote: When philosophy paints its grey in grey, one form of life has become old, and by means of grey it cannot be rejuvenated, but only known.
stops.quote_source: G.W.F. Hegel, Philosophy of Right, Preface, trans. S.W. Dyde (1896), marxists.org Hegel Archive
suggested_refs: Heinrich Heine, Zur Geschichte der Religion und Philosophie in Deutschland (1834), where the 'only one man understood me' story first appears and where Hegel is not dying

stops.name: Berlin, buried beside Fichte in the Dorotheenstadt ground
stops.date_confidence: 16 November 1831 attested. Two coordinate readings for the cemetery differ by about forty metres, 52.5293/13.3839 and 52.5296/13.3835; the first is used here and the second is recorded in the report.
stops.campa: He is buried in the Dorotheenstadt cemetery, in the ground he had asked for, between Johann Gottlieb Fichte and Karl Wilhelm Ferdinand Solger. Fichte held the Berlin chair before him and had been seventeen years dead; Solger taught in the same faculty. The three graves lie a few steps apart, and philosophy students still come and stand in front of them. Fifty-eight years on, the city will widen a street and the whole row will be lifted and set down deeper inside the same walls.
suggested_refs: The Dorotheenstädtischer Friedhof, Chausseestraße 126, Berlin-Mitte, graves of Hegel, Fichte and Solger

stops.name: Stuttgart, the drowning of Christiane
stops.date_confidence: 1832 attested. The place is given only as Württemberg in the sources consulted; the pin defaults to Stuttgart and claims nothing more. Month and day not established.
stops.campa: Christiane Hegel, the sister who was in the Stuttgart house when their mother died and who never married, drowns herself within months of her brother's death. She is the last of the three children of the Rentkammer secretary: the brother gone in Russia in 1812, the philosopher gone in Berlin in November, and now the sister in the water. The family that produced the system in which nothing is lost ends inside a single generation, in the duchy where it started.
suggested_refs: The death of Christiane Luise Hegel, 1832

stops.name: Berlin, the friends of the departed
stops.date_confidence: the society and its collected edition are attested in outline; the publication span, usually placed in the 1830s and 1840s, and the volume count could not be verified before the search budget ran out, and both remain reconstruction
stops.campa: A society of his friends and students, the Verein von Freunden des Verewigten, sets about printing everything: the books first, then the lectures, assembled out of student notebooks into volumes on aesthetics, on religion, on the philosophy of history that read as though he had written them himself. Karl and Immanuel hand over the papers. The Hegel the nineteenth century argues about is largely this edition, a voice reassembled by committee out of other men's handwriting.
stops.quote: Reason governs the world and has consequently governed its history.
stops.quote_source: G.W.F. Hegel, Introduction to the Philosophy of History, trans. Robert S. Hartman (1953), marxists.org Hegel Archive
suggested_refs: The Verein von Freunden des Verewigten and the first collected edition of Hegel's works
sources: General scholarly knowledge of Hegel reception history; no bibliographic source reached this session

stops.name: Berlin, Marx matriculates at the dead man's university
stops.date_confidence: 22 October 1836 per karl_marx.journey.json; the canonical Berlin university pin is inherited from that file unchanged
stops.campa: Karl Marx, eighteen, matriculates at the university on Unter den Linden, five years after the funeral and inside a faculty that is entirely Hegel's. Marx dislikes him at first. Convalescing at Stralau the following summer he reads him from end to end and is converted, and by 1841 he is at Hippel's wine cellar with the Doctors' Club among the Young Hegelians whom the new King means to drive out of every chair in Prussia. The dead man's argument is by now the only argument in Germany.
suggested_refs: The matriculation register of the Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität, October 1836

stops.name: Berlin, Schelling summoned against him
stops.date_confidence: 15 November 1841 per schelling.journey.json and humboldt.journey.json, which record the same event from both sides; the Berlin pin is inherited from schelling.journey.json unchanged
stops.campa: The King of Prussia calls the old Schelling out of Munich to the chair where Hegel taught and died, in so many words to root out the pantheism and the revolution grown from Hegel's school. Schelling is sixty-six and has been arguing with his Stift roommate for fifty years, ten of them since the roommate died. The hall at the inaugural lecture overflows: Kierkegaard, Engels, Bakunin, Burckhardt and Alexander von Humboldt are all in the room to hear one dead philosopher answered by the boy who shared his candle.
suggested_refs: Schelling's inaugural Berlin lecture of 15 November 1841 and the notebooks kept by Kierkegaard and Engels in the audience

stops.name: Berlin, the graves moved for a street
stops.date_confidence: 1889 attested by de.wikipedia; month and day not established
stops.campa: Berlin widens the Hannoversche Straße and the graves along that stretch of the Dorotheenstadt cemetery are in the way. Hegel's, Fichte's and Clemens Klenze's are taken up and set down again where they now stand, deeper inside the walls. The philosopher who argued that spirit keeps whatever it supersedes is moved by a road-widening scheme fifty-eight years after his funeral and stays, as he had asked, next to Fichte. The cemetery still holds them; the street runs where the older row stood.
suggested_refs: The 1889 relocation of graves at the Dorotheenstädtischer Friedhof for the widening of the Hannoversche Straße

stops.name: Stuttgart, the Hegel-Haus opens
stops.date_confidence: museum since 1991 and reopening on 27 August 2020, both attested; the month and day of the 1991 opening are not established
stops.campa: The house on the Eberhardstraße where he was born, a building of the sixteenth century, opens as the Hegel-Haus museum. It closes again for rebuilding and reopens on the twenty-seventh of August 2020, the two hundred and fiftieth birthday, its rooms labelled in German, English and Chinese. At Bochum the Hegel-Archiv, founded in 1958 and attached to the Ruhr University since 1968, goes on producing the critical edition volume by volume for the Academy and for the Meiner house at Hamburg.
suggested_refs: The Hegel-Haus, Eberhardstraße 53, Stuttgart
The Hegel-Archiv at the Ruhr-Universität Bochum and the Gesammelte Werke, Felix Meiner Verlag, Hamburg
